root_cause: The pre-review gate runner has a fixed 300 second subprocess timeout and the move-task hook always pays the gate cost before deciding whether enforcement or --force should matter. Timeout is an unverified/no-coverage condition, but the transition policy is not explicitly pinned for the advisory/default path and there is no supported timeout override, so large auto-derived scopes can consume the full hard-coded budget and surface as a failed pre-review gate instead of advisory evidence. The --force path is also sequenced after the run, so it cannot serve as an immediate bypass for an expensive or doomed gate.
approach: Add a small timeout resolver in `pre_review_gate.py` that reads `SPEC_KITTY_PRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT`, validates it as a positive integer, and falls back to the existing 300 second default; change the public timeout parameters to accept `None` so tests and callers can still pass explicit values while production uses the env-aware resolver. In `tasks_move_task.py`, short-circuit `_mt_run_pre_review_gate` when `st.force` is true by recording a skipped/no_coverage metadata payload and returning before workspace resolution, diffing, or pytest execution. Add an explicit regression around a timed-out advisory verdict proving the transition still emits policy metadata with `blocked: false`, and keep the only hard block as `block_enabled and outcome == NEW_FAILURES`.
tests_to_add: Unit test that `SPEC_KITTY_PRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT` is passed to `subprocess.run` and invalid/non-positive values fall back to 300 seconds.
Integration test where the pre-review evaluator returns a timeout/no_coverage verdict with `block_enabled` false and `move-task --to for_review` still commits the transition with `blocked: false`.
Integration or seam test proving `--force` skips the pre-review run entirely and records a force-bypassed/skipped metadata reason.
risk_notes: Changing timeout defaults from an integer literal to env-aware resolution touches several call sites; keep explicit timeout arguments behavior unchanged to avoid destabilizing existing tests.
out_of_scope_observations: The adjacent reviewer_agent attribution problem is a separate review-cycle metadata issue and should not be fixed in this PR.
